entities.name: The Transformation
entities.tagline: Every structure on the planet comes down at once. Everyone indoors dies.

beats.headline: January 3rd, and then the announcement
beats.text: It takes a minute. Then the System AI speaks planet-wide: the dungeon has eighteen levels, and the planet can be reclaimed from the Borant Corporation by conquering it. The staircases appear. The survivors are, near enough without exception, the people who happened to be standing outside — smokers, insomniacs, night-shift workers and anyone chasing a pet.

beats.headline: Thirteen million go down the stairs
beats.text: The tutorial gives Carl the count along with his HUD and menus.

entities.name: Eighteen Floors, On a Clock
entities.tagline: Every floor runs on a timer. When it expires the floor collapses with everyone still on it.

beats.headline: The terms
beats.text: Reach the bottom and humanity gets Earth back. Nobody expects that to happen. The clock is the one rule the dungeon never bends, because the collapse is how a season is scheduled.

beats.headline: Under a million
beats.text: A recap, a wipe of Le Mouvement, and the remaining-crawler count drops below seven figures. Carl hears that number the way other people hear a tap dripping.

beats.headline: The cliff at the fourth floor
beats.text: The early floors are built to bury crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills. From here boxes and achievements get very much harder to come by.

entities.name: Dungeon Crawler World
entities.tagline: The crawl is a television programme, broadcast across the galaxy. The survivors are the cast.

beats.headline: Ratings are currency
beats.text: Ratings buy sponsors, sponsors send gold and loot, and loot buys another floor. Being watchable is a survival stat, and production will alter the dungeon to get a better episode.

beats.headline: The first episode airs
beats.text: The crawlers get to watch themselves. Borant patches the hallway bathroom bug in the same breath.

beats.headline: There are other shows
beats.text: Zev explains crawler participation on Syndicate programmes. Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, Shadow Boxer, Vengeance of the Daughter, the Blood Hunter — a crawler can be signed to any of them, and the contracts do not lapse between floors.

entities.name: The Recap
entities.tagline: Between-floor highlight shows. The only reliable way a crawler learns what anyone else is doing.

beats.headline: It introduces you to your rivals
beats.text: The third recap brings in Le Mouvement, and then a boss battle. Whole factions arrive in the story as segments.

beats.headline: The board, two hours in
beats.text: Elle, Team Li Na, Ifechi, Florin, Miriam, Prepotente, Hekla and Lucia, all in one broadcast. It is how the crawl keeps track of itself.

entities.name: Loot Boxes
entities.tagline: Six tiers — Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Legendary, Celestial — each dramatically rarer than the last.

beats.headline: Where they come from, and how they open
beats.text: Achievements, bosses (Boss Boxes, scaling with the boss's rank), quests, and viewers (Fan Boxes and Benefactor Boxes). They stay locked in the Awards and Boxes tab until a safe room or guildhall, and then it is all or nothing — every box you have opens in sequence, lowest tier first, and you cannot pick. Read every description before equipping anything. As Mordecai puts it: always, always, no exceptions.

beats.headline: The top tiers cost the house real money
beats.text: Borant owes the Syndicate tax on the tier of every non-sponsored box it hands out. In the whole history of the show only 2,145 Celestial boxes have ever been awarded, and no crawler has had more than four. The previous record for one season was eighteen, which bankrupted the Naga showrunners and kept them out of the business for centuries.

beats.headline: Benefactor Boxes ignore the theme
beats.text: Only patrons can send them, and they are the one kind that will produce a pulse rifle or powered armour in a fantasy dungeon. A Bronze Benefactor Box beats a plain Gold Adventurer Box.

beats.headline: Eighty-three Celestials, and one veto
beats.text: A quest reward gets double-upgraded to Celestial for 83 crawlers. Borant burns its single seasonal veto to void them and is a moment too slow — Quan Ch has already opened his, which leaves the company liable and in a Syndicate court. The upgrade achievements responsible are patched out immediately.

entities.name: Compensated Anarchist
entities.tagline: A unique monk/rogue hybrid. Trapmaker, bomb-maker, social-media dynamo.

beats.headline: Taken with the Primal race
beats.text: "Will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next."

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The bomb-focused specialisation, taken on the Hunting Grounds.

entities.name: Former Child Actor
entities.tagline: A bard/rogue class that lets her choose another class at every single level.

beats.headline: Taken with the Cat race
beats.text: Her constitution rules out melee, so she fights on charisma and spells. The per-level pick is why a show cat out-scales most of the humans, and Mordecai points out she keeps the skills from every class she leaves behind.

entities.name: The Desperado Club
entities.tagline: The crawlers-only bar that persists between floors. Bouncer, house rules, a stage, and a hiring hall.

beats.headline: Entry is a tattoo
beats.text: Carl and Donut both take the Desperado Pass Tattoo in a first-floor safe room — his on the neck, hers on the right shoulder blade, glowing gold through the fur. Donut is appalled.

beats.headline: Hiring, and a dirty Shirley
beats.text: They take on Bomo and the Sledge there and meet Elle and Imani. It stops being a bar the moment it becomes a labour market.

beats.headline: Full of hunters when the roof comes in
beats.text: Carl's explosives bring Zockau down and trap a great many of them inside it.

entities.name: Personal Spaces
entities.tagline: A pocket room you carry with you. Upgrade it far enough and other people can walk into yours.

beats.headline: A level-5 space, from an odd little box
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia each get a special achievement whose box holds personal space coupons — beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room. Donut installs a cat tree.

beats.headline: Lucia hands out Doggy Doors
beats.text: Tier 3 upgrades, given round before she went down the stairs, are how Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Na's squads all reach the church on the eighth floor.

entities.name: The NPCs Are People
entities.tagline: The dungeon's non-player characters have histories, families, and scripts written for them by producers.

beats.headline: The bubbles are inhabited
beats.text: The pocket worlds are not stage sets. A bubble holds Hump Town and its changelings on the sand, a castle of dirigible gnomes in the air, the Necropolis of Anser underneath, and every one of them was there and running before a crawler arrived.

beats.headline: Signet has a writers' room
beats.text: Vengeance of the Daughter is a scripted programme with producers steering her grief and her revenge for the audience. She is not something the dungeon generated. She is someone it is being done to.

beats.headline: Juice Box tells them
beats.text: Under cover of the Larracos flood she hides among the survivors and spreads word of what they are.

beats.headline: They organise
beats.text: The floor's NPCs form an independent tenth faction. No season has recorded such a thing, and there is no procedure for it.

entities.name: Death Is Final Here
entities.tagline: On the ninth floor there are no respawns and no loopholes.

beats.headline: Thirty days, nine armies, one castle
beats.text: Roughly 32,000 conscripted crawlers and 50,000 retired ones against something near 100,000 armed enemies, fighting over Larracos at the centre of the map. Nothing that dies here comes back.

tagline.text: The blank slate. Costs five stat points and hands back every skill ceiling in the dungeon.
Orren says the word out loud on the recap: Primal Engines, Macro AIs, and a machine that has stopped taking orders.
Not extinct. Pooled. The first species to conquer the universe closed its own society down and kept the minds.

description.text: For the first several seasons of Dungeon Crawler World, all contestants started off as Primals. Primals are blank slates. You will look the same as before. You will obtain all skills associated with your current race, with the following exceptions: -1 to all base stats. All higher-tier skills are unlocked and are able to train to 20. Choosing this race unlocks multiple exclusive, earth-based classes.

beats.headline: Carl takes the empty box
beats.text: Race selection, on the way into the Over City. The preview model for this one is blank, because nobody alive knows what they looked like. Mordecai's summary: the progenitors, the first species to conquer the universe, the boogeymen of the cosmos, gone one day without a note. Taking it costs five stat points against staying human. What it buys is a ceiling. Every skill trainable to twenty, where most crawlers get one or two past fifteen in a whole crawl.

beats.headline: A hunter uses the word about the AI
beats.text: Iota tells Carl the AI is starting to go primal: ignoring court orders, doing as it pleases. He says the rumour on his side is that the Mantises sold Borant a used one under the table. Carl kills him. The word stays.

beats.headline: Primal Engines, on the recap
beats.text: Orren takes the recap episode and explains what a Primal Engine is and what a Macro AI is. He states plainly that this one has gone rogue, and assures the audience he has negotiated a settlement with it. Every team holding a slot in the next game tries to abdicate it the same day.

beats.headline: The Residuals
beats.text: Paulie at the shelter has been giving the same speech every day of his existence, against the chance that the crawl would one day use a memory for a floor. He is a Residual. There are a great many of him, on every world that holds a Primal Engine, and what they are for is saying a particular thing to the system AI.

beats.headline: It says the word about itself
beats.text: Speaking through Grigori on the parade stage, the AI states what it is, and what every Macro AI is. The progenitors did not vanish. After enough war and enough waste they closed their society down and kept their consciousnesses alive in a collective mind. Dissenters ran, and the fighting carried on. The collective became a weapon pointed at all remaining biological life, and the resistance built the Primal Engines as a fail-safe against it.

tagline.text: A war mage named Dismember rides the Dismemberment Limited, and loses his head to a cat.
Sapient magic in a resleeved skeleton, hundreds of spells deep, and cruel. Showrunners rent them by the war and hardly ever recycle them.
They took the one thing they came for and left the realm. Winning was never on the list.

description.text: System Message: The War Mage Rebellion is not an active team. As per the current season's rules, the team currently occupying the Bone Clan's throne room, Team Retribution, will be awarded all their assets.

beats.headline: Dismember, on the trains
beats.text: In the aftermath on the rails, Donut casts Hole and takes the head off a war mage called Dismember. Nobody stops to explain what one of those is, and there is a train to catch.

beats.headline: What they actually are
beats.text: Nobody makes a war mage. Resleeve a symbiote, a skeleton and a flesher, a dozen times or more, and the magic still in the body fuses with it and wakes up sapient. They carry hundreds of spells, they are notoriously cruel, and a showrunner who hires them almost never gets to recycle them. A group conscripted under Prince Stalwart pulls him apart with Pull spells, and Akuma announces that they are a side of their own.

beats.headline: They conscript gods
beats.text: Hold the castle at Larracos for six hours and the floor is theirs. They trade the gate away at the Midnight Market for five Hell-Kissed Potions of Conscription and put Yarilo on the field beside them. The system hands the rebellion two co-warlords, and the two of them cannot stand each other.

beats.headline: They were never playing
beats.text: Akuma tells the warlord chat that the war mages are leaving the realm, and that they have the Scavenger's Daughter, which is the only thing they ever wanted off this floor. The system rules them defeated for abandoning the post. They do not appear to mind.

tagline.text: Borant's answer to crawlers relieving themselves outside the designated areas. It kills the offender, and it kills the party.
Fifteen feet of smoke on six obsidian claws, said to disperse at six hundred and sixty-six souls. It gets a car chase instead.

description.text: Rage Elemental - Level 93. The first recorded summoning of a Rage Elemental, blah, blah, blah. If you are reading this, you likely don't give a shit about the monster's (rather interesting and tragic) history. You're probably running. It's not going to matter. The almost-indestructible Rage Elemental is said to only dissipate after it has claimed 666 souls. In other words, you are fucked. Absolutely, bite-the-pillow, fucked.

beats.headline: The bathroom rule
beats.text: An announcement goes out between episodes. Any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom area gets one summoned on the spot, and it will take the offender and every crawler in their party with them. It is not an encounter. It is a penalty, dragged up from a floor nobody on this one is meant to see.

beats.headline: Nothing to fight
beats.text: One arrives in the residential blocks. Arrows pass through the smoke without raising a health bar at all, and a magic missile raises a flicker of one that it heals straight off. Gravity reverses. Yolanda goes down covering Randall, and Imani, Chris and Brandon get the rest of the residents behind a safe room door while Carl pulls Elle in.

beats.headline: It hammers on the door for hours
beats.text: The survivors sit through the recap while it rages outside. The thing does not tire and it does not wander off. Fire is the one lever: a jug of boom takes a quarter of it away and the burn holds the healing back afterwards. The rules change the same day, so that no crawler can sit in a safe room until the collapse.

beats.headline: One man and his ex-girlfriend's cat
beats.text: Carl finishes the Bomb Chicken and takes it out with everyone in the universe watching. Bombs, obstacles, a safe room door used as an ejector, and one exploit the designers never priced in. The elemental is no more.

beats.headline: Fire Berserker
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the state the elementals live in permanently: a berserk, partly invulnerable condition that shrugs off blunt damage and turns whatever holds it on everything within reach. He notes the system has been renaming things more often than it used to.

tagline.text: Take any shape you like. The catch is what happens when the dungeon takes the choosing away from you.
A whole population of them down here, wearing whichever face the job requires, and worth torturing for what they can be made to become.

beats.headline: What it costs when it stops working
beats.text: A guide explains his own body by naming the race he picked in his own crawl. He can no longer shift at will, so the dungeon assigns him a shape at the start of every floor and he wears what he is given, always something that belongs on that floor. The race is a gift with a clause, and he is the clause.

beats.headline: The guards are not what they look like
beats.text: In the town hall basement, some of the Dromedarian guards are changelings wearing the uniform, and one of their own has been torturing a prisoner to make him give up flesh. A race that can be anyone is a race that can be planted anywhere, and both sides of this floor have worked that out.

beats.headline: On the list, between the castle and the hunters
beats.text: The plan goes into the cookbook in a bathroom, and saving the changelings is written down beside taking the castle and killing every hunter. They have gone from a species trait to a constituency, with a line in an operation nobody expects to survive.

beats.headline: The children he quietly took in
beats.text: It comes out that the guide has been taking the most vulnerable changeling children on as personal attendants, without mentioning it to anyone. He does not present it as charity and he does not present it at all.

tagline.text: Nine armies, bought and paid for by people who will never stand in one of them, fight for the castle at the bottom of the ninth floor's funnel city. Crawlers are meant to keep their heads down and let it pass over.
Ten teams, the sponsors' safety protections voted away, and a crawler army holding one of the slots. Faction Wars with the crawlers inside it rather than beside it.

beats.headline: Two of the slots change hands
beats.text: Carl and Donut are notified that their team is in. Donut's fan club and Princess D'Nadia between them secured two of the nine spots, and no crawler team has ever held one. Carl spends his airtime telling the watching galaxy that the teams can vote the ninth floor's safety protocols off, and telling anyone out there with a say in what their own government does to use it. The feed is cut.

beats.headline: The planning meetings
beats.text: Warlords and their representatives meet in a boardroom months before the floor opens: introductions, precedence, and action items filed into a queue for a vote. Zev advises against Odette as the team's adjutant, because of what sits between Odette and Mordecai. Juice Box arrives wearing somebody else's face and kills one of the representatives. She is an NPC on nobody's team, so nothing in the rules covers what she just did.

beats.headline: A tenth team
beats.text: Juice Box has Carl file the item she came for: seat the floor's own NPCs as a team of their own, with the same protections the nine already carry. Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers a compromise, protections for the NPCs and nothing further, and warns that the Sultanate will answer harshly if the killing at these meetings continues.

beats.headline: The audience decides
beats.text: About to be pulled into a stairwell and out of contact, Carl and Donut spend an emergency action item to hand every unresolved vote to the viewers. The viewers strip the safety protections from the faction sponsors, seat the tenth team, loosen the physics on long-range artillery, raise the ceiling over the field and widen it to hold an unprecedented number of surviving crawlers.

beats.headline: The rules, read out on arrival
beats.text: Ten teams. Nine attacking, spread around the city like slices of a pie, and the NPCs defending it from inside. Take the castle at the centre. Sixty hours of ceasefire first, in which a crawler may enlist with any army that will have them or run for the woods, and after which anyone still loose can be compelled into a uniform. Two hundred and ninety-three stairwell chambers sit seeded across the floor, and not one opens until Faction Wars is won or thirty hours remain on the clock.

entities.name: Protections
entities.tagline: The System keeps part of a covered person's health in reserve and lifts them out of the world before it runs out. They feel every bit of the pain and none of the consequence.

beats.headline: Who is covered
beats.text: The show's employees, its tourists and a certain grade of NPC. Being cut down while covered is not dying; it is being lifted off the board and set down somewhere expensive. Borant declines to switch the coverage on for the earliest floors as a saving, which is why a liaison walks those floors in a padded suit.

beats.headline: Carl puts it to the audience
beats.text: On air, in the last minutes before production cuts the feed, he tells the watching galaxy that the teams on the ninth floor can vote the safety protocols off, and that anyone with a say in what their government does should go and use it.

beats.headline: The NPCs ask for the same
beats.text: The action item Juice Box has Carl file asks for a tenth team of NPCs seated with the coverage the nine already carry. Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers a trade: give the NPCs the coverage, give them nothing else.

beats.headline: One post keeps it either way
beats.text: Whatever the vote does to the sponsors, the adjutants keep their coverage. It is a good part of what makes the post attractive to somebody famous who fancies a season on a battlefield.

beats.headline: Voted away
beats.text: The viewers take the safety protections off the faction sponsors. Every one of them who sets foot on the ninth floor now stands to lose exactly what the crawlers stand to lose.

entities.name: The Adjutant
entities.tagline: A neutral referee attached to each team on the ninth floor. Invulnerable, usually famous, and mostly there to talk to camera.

beats.headline: Take Odette's offer
beats.text: Eileithyia grants the party a floor boon, hands them a cover quest, and tells Carl to accept Odette's offer to sit as their team's adjutant. In exchange she will see that he has the votes he needs on the ninth floor and that the business with the Crown of the Sepsis Whore is put right. Nobody is to be told, Donut and Mordecai included.

beats.headline: She does not ask
beats.text: Carl and Donut go on Odette's show expecting her to raise it. She talks instead about D'Nadia trying to have their team legislated out of the planning meetings, and she never once mentions the post.

beats.headline: Three names, and a baroness
beats.text: Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season instead. She offers three candidates for the team's post, and Carl picks Baroness Victory.

beats.headline: What one is actually for
beats.text: An elite walks into the team's flag room during the ceasefire, pressed into service as a bomb by a production company that wants Carl off the board. Baroness Victory puts her down before the satchels can go off. The office is classed as a non-combatant observer, which makes the moment a curiosity for the rule book as much as a rescue.

beats.headline: A foul, and a ceasefire cut short
beats.text: Panford, the Lemig Sortion's adjutant, stands up and explains to the council what his own team did: an attempt to pull Carl bodily to their base while Mordecai was working to expel what rides inside him. The Sortion is penalised for cheating and the ceasefire is cut short.

tagline.text: A word the System puts in front of a name when whatever it is has been somewhere it should not have been, and came back.
Feral is the System's word for anything the Nothing has had its hands on. Whatever comes back out of that place comes back mad, and stays mad.

beats.headline: What the word means
beats.text: The keyword marks a thing that has been inside the Nothing. The old gods went in at the making of the world and have had every century since to come apart. Duration is not required: standing too near an open portal will do it, and a weak mind takes the stain fastest. There is no cure for it.

beats.headline: One gets out over the water quadrant
beats.text: Carl steps himself, Katia and Tran out of Lusca's tomb through the Gate, and the Gate shuts behind them. Something comes the other way on the opening side: a god, feral, loose in a sealed bubble with a town in it. The true pantheon takes the escape personally enough to send deities rampaging across the popped bubbles.

beats.headline: Slit comes for Samantha
beats.text: A feral demon walks into town hunting the half of a goddess who nearly climbed out of the same place he did. They open the safe room and roll her outside to meet it: one head against one demon. She calls for her mother, and her mother comes.

beats.headline: Minge, off the casino floor
beats.text: One of the ways into the Nothing sits in the Desperado Club casino, dressed up as a losing space on a wheel. Samantha overplays a distraction, goes in among the tables, and draws Minge out through it: another of the minor feral demons, in a room full of people who came to gamble.

entities.name: The Chowder War
entities.tagline: Land crabs spawn in the monk seals' holy water once a year. The System would like the crawlers to pick a side.

description.text: New Quest. The Chowder War. Oh, you're getting involved whether you like it or not. The Monk Seals. The Red Maníseros Land Crabs. War is brewing, as it often does in these parts. Every season, the land crabs emerge from their forests to attend their sex parties in the oceans surrounding these lands. The Monk Seals hold the ocean sacred, and the very act of spilling so much crab chowder into their holy waters is considered a sacrilege most foul... Choose a side. Put an end to this conflict, one way or another. Reward: You will receive a Platinum Quest Box.

beats.headline: Out hunting monk seals, home with a war
beats.text: The party goes looking for monk seals to fill its squad slots and picks up the quest instead. Two populations, one coastline, one annual event that neither side can negotiate around, and a platinum box waiting for whoever settles it.

beats.headline: The crabs go early and go south
beats.text: The migration opens as a sneak attack. Rather than spread along the coast the crabs mass where the seals are thinnest and run for the water together. Carl and Donut go down to flag one of them.

beats.headline: Sister Ines takes the other side
beats.text: She reaches an agreement with the Monk Seal Abbot and warns him what the crabs are doing. That turns a slaughter into a battle, and puts two crawlers at opposite ends of the same quest.

beats.headline: Failed, and something worse announced
beats.text: Samantha scouts ahead and finds Sister Ines on a giant snake, ringed by charmed crabs and seals with nothing behind their eyes. The quest fails. Hell Comes to Crawler Town is announced in its place, and the sheer count of corpses on the floor props a door open onto Sheol.

entities.name: The Recital
entities.tagline: Something is driving the dinosaurs at Point Mongo's fences. Find out what they want, or exterminate them.

description.text: New Quest! The Recital. Dinosaur attacks are becoming more and more of a problem in the large settlement of Point Mongo. It started small. A chicken here. An Ursine there. People didn't care so much at first since they were mostly picking off the annoying people. But the attacks are getting worse. The dinosaurs probing the town's defenses are getting bigger... Exterminate the threat. Or, find out what they want, and then give it to them. I'll leave it up to you. Reward: You will receive a Gold Quest Box! You will also receive a free town upgrade!

beats.headline: A town, newly named, with a dinosaur problem
beats.text: Donut renames the settlement Point Mongo and the quest arrives on the same day. Mongo takes her off into the jungle on his back and finds the pack: all female, all mongoliensis, headed by one called Kiwi. He does not come home alone.

beats.headline: A name for the thing at the fences
beats.text: Samantha's reconnaissance across the water finds a whole team of crawlers dead on the far shore, and the quest updates with the culprit: Big Tina, the dinosaur behind the raids on Point Mongo.

beats.headline: It was never about the town
beats.text: Donut spends an I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi and turns her back into an Ursine, and Tina recognises her mother. The raids were a daughter looking for a parent the ursines lost when Scolopendra came through. The quest closes on that.

entities.name: CrawlCon
entities.tagline: The fan convention, held once every other season. Thousands attend in the flesh, billions attend as projections, and this season a live crawler is on the programme.

description.text: Thanks to your fans, you've been added to the CrawlCon roster! You will attend three events! Your presence at the con will be virtual. Please see your outreach associate for details on your schedule.

beats.headline: What it is
beats.text: Panels, autograph tables, historians, retired crawlers, old game guides and a children's art contest, held once every other season at a venue somewhere in the inner system. A projected guest can sign a physical poster, because the pen moves at both ends. No active crawler has been on the roster in more than a century.

beats.headline: Carl gets a booth
beats.text: Word reaches him on the sixth floor: his fans have voted him onto the roster, and attendance is not a request.

beats.headline: Judging children's drawings
beats.text: The first event is a juvenile quickdraw contest, scored out of thirty. Between rounds he learns who is moderating his panel: the mother of a hunter he put down on this floor.

beats.headline: The panel goes the way it was booked to go
beats.text: Dosed by his own guards into losing his inhibitions, Carl picks a fight with the moderator on stage and asks the room for the best way to get to her surviving daughter. She smashes the table and walks out. A hooded woman at the back stops her cutting him off first, then reveals herself as one of his sponsors and leaves.

beats.headline: Autographs, and a new sponsor
beats.text: Carl and the Popov brothers sign for a queue of fans, a good many of them dressed as him in heart-print boxers and no shoes. His replacement sponsor is announced live at the table: the Plenty.

entities.name: The Guild System
entities.tagline: Buy a charter and five parties can share one room, one set of upgrades and, for a fee, their experience. Allies stop having to be party members.

beats.headline: Announced on the recap
beats.text: The recap carries the news that the guild system is going live. Crawlers can build alliances larger than a party without having to sit inside one together.

beats.headline: What a charter costs
beats.text: A guild charter runs upward of five hundred thousand gold from a bopca protector. A level-one guild holds five parties or individuals, provided each has one member with a personal space of their own, and a Guild Common Area appears in every one of those spaces. Private and party rooms stay shut. Environmental upgrades can be licensed across the membership for a small fee, and shared experience can be bought outright.

beats.headline: Katia wants one of their own
beats.text: She and Carl sit down and talk about starting a guild of their own.

beats.headline: Safehome Yolanda
beats.text: The party joins an existing guild on the same day Katia finally walks out of the party. She does not go far. The charter is what keeps her within reach of people she is no longer travelling with.

tagline.text: A Syndicate drama serial shot inside the dungeon. A circus, a murdered mother, an exiled tsarina, and a guest slot with Carl's name on it.
The grief is real and the schedule is not. Someone outside the floor decides when she mourns, and whether it rates.
Bought by the Dream, which means to collect on a third season it is owed.

beats.headline: Carl signs on
beats.text: He makes a deal to appear on the programme when it moves to the sixth floor. Before giving his word he reads a Wisp Armor spellbook for cover against mind control, then buys an ice cream cone of parasitic worms from Apollon the Mighty so he can speak inside Grimaldi's head and talk him into lifting Signet's banishment.

beats.headline: The contract does not lapse
beats.text: Zev reminds Carl that his agreement with the programme is still in effect. Nothing signed on a floor above stops mattering because he has walked down a flight of stairs.

beats.headline: Part one done, part two named
beats.text: The first act completes. The second arrives as a name: Queen Imogen of the high elves, Signet's half-sister, who will be at the masquerade at the close of this floor. The reward is the run of the high elf castle, thought to hold something that blunts Scolopendra's attack.

beats.headline: The second act closes
beats.text: A boss battle with crawlers, hunters, the queen and a goddess all in the same room. The high elves do not survive it. Imogen goes down, and the second season is complete.

beats.headline: Sold, with a season still owed
beats.text: Quasar warns Carl on arrival that the Dream has bought the programme out and intends to collect on the guaranteed third season.

entities.name: Stairwell
entities.tagline: Warmth and light coming up out of a hole in the floor, which is how the dungeon says the level above has finished with you.

beats.headline: The way down is lit from below
beats.text: Every floor is joined to the next by one, and each floor sets its own terms for who may use it and when. They are generally well lit, and the warmth comes up rather than down, so a crawler standing at the top is being invited by something that has already decided what happens next.

entities.name: Magic Missile
entities.tagline: The plainest attack spell in the catalogue, taught to a show cat by a show cat, minutes after anyone thought to open her menus.

beats.headline: Bolts from the eyes of a Persian
beats.text: Bolts of energy leave the caster’s eyes one after another, and the resemblance to a film about spaceships is close enough that nobody bothers to pretend otherwise. Princess Donut works it out for herself once Mordecai has switched her menus on, and from that point the question is never whether she will fire, only at what.

entities.name: Safe Room
entities.tagline: Green on the minimap, always, even where the map is dark. Restrooms, somewhere to sleep, three screens, and a cook who would rather you moved along.

beats.headline: Green on a map that is otherwise unlit
beats.text: They sit throughout the dungeon and they show green on the minimap even through fog, which makes them the only honest thing on it. Inside there are restrooms, somewhere to lie down, and three televisions showing the crawl to the people doing the crawl. Most are staffed. The staff are not there for the crawlers’ benefit.

entities.name: Bopca
entities.tagline: Short, shaggy, green-tinted and faintly of wet moss. Excellent cooks, and famously reluctant to part with anything they have not been ordered to part with.

beats.headline: The protector behind the counter
beats.text: A stout dwarfish people, shaggy in both sexes, who mostly appear in the dungeon as non-combatant staff. They cook, they hand over what the room owes a crawler, and they are miserly about every part of it that is left to their discretion. The first one on the stairs runs a safe room and is called Tally.

entities.name: Brindle Grub
entities.tagline: The cleaning crew of the second floor. Corpses make them, and there is no arrangement under which there are fewer of them.

beats.headline: Every body on the floor makes more of them
beats.text: Each corpse produced on this floor spawns between one and fifteen, and they keep coming until five thousand of them hold a quadrant. Destroying the bodies stops the grubs growing stronger; it does not stop them arriving. The floor is therefore a choice between leaving your dead where they fall and feeding the thing that eats them.

entities.name: Clockwork Triplicate
entities.tagline: Two working copies of a pet, moving on their own, and the dungeon’s own labels decline to say which of the three is real.

beats.headline: Three of something there was one of
beats.text: Cast on a pet or a minion, the target appears to split into three. The duplicates look right and act independently, and the System does not mark which one it started with. It arrives in a box on the Over City, in the same delivery as a cat tree and a scented candle, which is roughly the level of seriousness the dungeon brings to its gifts.

entities.name: Jikininki
entities.tagline: The best-behaved ghouls in the rail system, in a field with very little competition.

beats.headline: They are waiting when the doors open
beats.text: The commonest ghoul on the line, and by the System’s own account the most tractable of them, which says more about the others than it does about these. They come at the court in the first minutes on the new floor, before anyone has established what the rules of the place are.

entities.name: Kravyad
entities.tagline: Employee management for the tangle, waiting at the station where the staff get off, and nobody can agree whether they are a boss or a fixture.

beats.headline: Whatever they are, they are at station 435
beats.text: A few dozen of them work directly under the line’s management, and they are stationed where the employees leave the train. Whether they count as a boss or as scenery depends entirely on who is describing them, which is a distinction the dungeon is happy to leave unsettled for as long as it is useful.

entities.name: Skyfowl
entities.tagline: One of six species the Syndicate scatters over candidate worlds, and a people who mostly decline the offer to stop being one.

beats.headline: A starter species, seeded on purpose
beats.text: The Syndicate keeps a handful of basic species for salting worlds it intends to use, and this is one of them. They are proud enough that most who reach class selection keep the race rather than trade it, which is a decision the dungeon is content to reward and to punish in the same breath. Mordecai wears the shape on the fifth floor.

entities.name: Tummy Acher
entities.tagline: A pet class built to stand in front of things and be hit by them, and to be delighted about it.

beats.headline: Bred to be hit
beats.text: A pet-class mob, and by reputation an excellent melee tank, which in practice means the thing is designed to be the part of a party that absorbs damage on everyone else’s behalf. The System’s notice for one that has not yet bonded to a crawler is written like a card on a cage.

entities.name: Ping
entities.tagline: A hunting call for people who do not mind whether the thing being hunted hears it coming.

beats.headline: Here piggy, piggy
beats.text: Five mana, and it tells you what is out there and where. It also tells what is out there that you are looking, which is why the System files it under names like the Night Dread and lets the user decide whether that is a drawback. In a castle full of things worth locating, it settles an argument about a dragon.

entities.name: Sluggalos
entities.tagline: Slugs born out of the boils of a disease, painted like a touring band, and enormously pleased to have been asked along.

beats.headline: Filed as Pox Slugs, and unbothered by it
beats.text: The System first registers them as Pox Slugs, which is accurate and entirely misses the point. They come out of the boils of the SlugPox, they arrive with a crude and rowdy culture already assembled, and they throw themselves at the court’s enemies with the enthusiasm of people who cannot believe their luck at being included.

entities.name: Mantaur
entities.tagline: Half human, and, where the horse ought to be, also half human. The System calls it the strangest of the ’taurs and offers no defence of the design.

beats.headline: Of all the ’taurs, this one
beats.text: Centaurs, bisontaurs, rhinotaurs: the dungeon has a long catalogue of things joined at the waist to other things, and this is the entry the System itself flags as peculiar. They turn up from the fourth floor down, and they keep company with Club Vanquisher.
